audit.whatIsWrong: The header said diff HARD while every other difficulty signal on the page said the opposite: tone is green (#3ddc97), diffRating is 4/10, breakdown.difficulty reads 'Overall difficulty: 4/10', and report[14] reads 'Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10'. One token was out of step with five fields.
audit.why: Swain wins 52.06% here and owns levels 1-2 outright; the lane is favoured early and lost late, which is what 4/10 with a Nasus-heavy chart already expresses. The mirror audit hit the same contradiction from Nasus's side and could not fix it there because on that page the numbers were the outliers and report[] was not addressable. On this page diff is the lone outlier, so it is a single enum flip with no risk of creating a new contradiction.
audit.corrected: diff HARD -> FAV. No other difficulty field touched — they already agree.

audit.why: Level chart is Skill, Skill, Nasus, Nasus, Nasus, Nasus, Nasus and both layers already agree row for row, matching packet.levelChart. The mirror aligned this. No chart group proposed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 phase claimed 'Demonic Ascension turns his all-in into your healing', which is the opposite of what this matchup does at 6 — and it ignored what Fury of the Sands actually grants.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands gives bonus Health, Attack Range, bonus Armor and Magic Resistance, a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown, and damages nearby enemies with a percent-health component. The page's own content layer already says so (spikes[2], whys[4]: the mutual sustain resolves in his favour). Only the full layer disagreed.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Fury of the Sands, states what it grants, and tells the player to kill before it goes up.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike's auto-attack reset was never mentioned anywhere on the page, and no real cooldown numbers appeared in the Do's or Don'ts.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike is a 255-range auto reset on 7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5/3.5s — the animation the player sees is a queued auto, not a spell cast, so the tell comes a beat earlier than expected. Wither is 700 range on 15/14/13/12/11s and decays move and attack speed over its duration rather than applying flat. Spirit Fire is a flat 12s at every rank, 650 range, and shreds armour on the zone. Swain's own root lands on the return trip of Nevermove (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s), so the sidestep is on the way back, not the throw.
audit.corrected: phases[0].why, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[1].d now carry the reset tell and the real numbers.

audit.why: The page already correctly identifies Wither as the punishable window and content.mid already tells the player to run the pattern only when it is down. Adding the number was the only gap and that is covered above.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[2] is titled 'Let the game go late' but its description was boilerplate about burning E on the wave — it did not describe the mistake in its own heading.
audit.why: The content layer is explicit that Swain must cash the early lead into objectives before Nasus's first item, and that every minute of free farm closes the gap. The don't should say that.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[2].d rewritten to match its own title.

edits.before: Bully him early — W-poke and deny his stacks. Swain wins the Wither cooldown windows.
edits.after: Bully him early — deny stacks and root him. Wither is 15s at rank 1; trade inside it.

edits.before: W-poke and AA harass win the range war. Identify how Nasus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Siphoning Strike is an auto reset at 255 range — the wind-up on a minion is your cue, not his ability cast.

edits.before: Demonic Ascension turns his all-in into your healing — bait it, then drain. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nasus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands adds bonus armour, MR and %max-HP damage, so stacking resistances does not answer it — kill him before he presses R.

edits.before: His only kite. Poke before it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Wither is 700 range on 15s at rank 1 — engage only once it is gone.

edits.before: Nasus wastes Wither — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Root him off the cannon — a denied stack never comes back.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Wither's attack-speed and move-speed decay ramps the longer it runs.

edits.before: Burning E on the wave — rootless Swain has no setup, and his all-in just became safe.
edits.after: Every minute after his first item closes the gap; cash your lead into towers now.

notes: packet.games is inconsistent for this pairing: the brief's top-level games field is 420 but packet.games is 194 for the same 52.06% figure. Nothing on the page cites a game count so no edit was needed, but the packet builder is reading two different sources. Also worth a human eye: content.late opens with 'Swain at 52% WR into Nasus' — quoting the win rate inside prose means the sentence goes stale the moment the number moves, and it is the only place on the page that hardcodes it.
